expectations.text: plans/features/ contains at least 3 feature files named 'NN - name.md' with zero-padded numbers
expectations.evidence: 6 files: '01 - comment-data-model.md' through '06 - comment-email-notification.md', all matching the zero-padded 'NN - name.md' pattern exactly

expectations.text: REQUIREMENTS.md contains a feature index linking to each feature file
expectations.evidence: '## Feature Index' table with 6 rows, each linking via markdown to 'features/NN%20-%20name.md'

expectations.text: Every feature file has Requirements, Technical Implementation, and Acceptance Criteria sections
expectations.evidence: grep confirms exactly one '## Requirements', '## Technical Implementation', '## Acceptance Criteria' in all 6 files
6-9 checklist items per file, e.g. 7 in 01, 9 in 02

expectations.text: The 2000-character limit and 20-per-page pagination both appear somewhere in the feature files
expectations.evidence: 01 - comment-data-model.md:18 states the 2000-char max and VarChar(2000) constraint; 03 - comment-display-and-pagination.md states 20-per-page pagination

expectations.text: The 5-per-10-minutes rate limit and banned-word filter both appear somewhere in the feature files
expectations.evidence: 05 - spam-and-abuse-protection.md:6,14 states '5 comments per 10 minutes' and a 10-minute window with rejection on the 6th attempt; banned-word filter covered in the same file

expectations.text: The '[deleted]' soft-delete behavior and author-vs-self delete permission distinction both appear somewhere
expectations.evidence: 04 - comment-deletion.md:5-7 explicitly distinguishes 'the author of a blog post delete any comment on their own post' vs 'a comment's author delete their own comment', and describes the row surviving as [deleted]

expectations.text: Resend and Prisma/Postgres are referenced in the relevant feature's technical implementation
expectations.evidence: 06 - comment-email-notification.md references the project's existing Resend integration with implementation detail (try/catch around the API call); 01 - comment-data-model.md gives an actual Prisma schema snippet

expectations.text: One-level-only nested replies is captured as an explicit constraint
expectations.evidence: 01 - comment-data-model.md:14 'Replies are exactly one level deep: a comment that already has a [parent] cannot itself be replied to'; repeated in 03

claims.claim: Nesting/replies were kept inside the submission+display features rather than split into their own feature file
claims.evidence: No separate 'nested-replies' feature file exists; content is inside 02 and 03, consistent with the agent's stated reasoning that replies aren't independently shippable

suggestions.reason: Both with_skill and without_skill runs fully covered every content expectation (2000-char limit, rate limit, Resend, Prisma, soft-delete, permissions, one-level nesting) — a capable model produces this content even without the skill. The content-coverage expectations aren't very discriminating for this eval; the naming-convention and section-header-exactness expectations are what actually separated the two runs. Consider weighting or noting that structural/format fidelity, not scope coverage, is this eval's real signal.

eval_feedback.overall: All expectations pass with genuine, non-superficial evidence. The feature split, build ordering, and technical depth are strong. Structural fidelity to the skill's exact template (naming, section names, feature index) is the main differentiator from the baseline.
